concepts.title: Machine Learning Model Accuracy
concepts.definition: Machine learning is the branch of artificial intelligence where a program builds its own model from example data instead of following hand-written rules; after training, the model is scored by the share of test cases it gets right.
concepts.key_idea: A model earns trust only when its score on unseen testing data crosses the accepted accuracy bar.
question_patterns: A trained model answered 92 of 100 test cases correctly. Find its accuracy percentage.
Out of 250 predictions a model made, 30 were wrong. Compute the accuracy in percent.
How does machine learning differ from ordinary programming?
Why is a model tested on separate testing data after training?
A spam filter reaches 97 percent accuracy on 500 mails. How many mails did it classify correctly?
Name two everyday applications powered by machine learning.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the correct predictions by all predictions made.
Multiply the share by 100 to report accuracy.

worked_examples.q: A trained model gets 45 test cases right out of 50. What is its accuracy in percent?

concepts.title: Five Characteristics of Big Data
concepts.definition: Datasets too bulky or messy for ordinary database tools are called big data; they are judged on five traits: sheer volume, speed of arrival (velocity), mix of formats (variety), trustworthiness (veracity) and the useful knowledge hidden inside (value).
concepts.formula: judge(data) on volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value
concepts.key_idea: Volume alone is not enough; how fast data arrives, how mixed and how reliable it is decides whether it is truly big data.
question_patterns: List the five characteristics of big data and explain any two.
A hospital stream gains sensor readings every millisecond. Which characteristic of big data does this rate illustrate?
Photos, tweets and tables mixed in one dataset illustrate which trait of big data?
What does veracity tell us about a dataset?
Why might a huge dataset still be worthless to a business?
Why can conventional DBMS tools fail on big data?

solution_steps.action: check the dataset against the five traits
solution_steps.explain: Estimate its size, arrival rate, format mix and reliability, and look for hidden patterns that would repay the processing cost.

worked_examples.q: Which of the five big-data traits describes the speed at which data arrives?

concepts.title: Sizing Daily Big Data Generation
concepts.definition: Web users, phones and connected gadgets produce data on a colossal scale each day; expressing the daily flood in familiar storage units shows why special processing systems are needed.
concepts.key_idea: Roughly 2.5 quintillion bytes arise every day, which is a few exabytes and far beyond a single machine.
question_patterns: About 2.5 quintillion bytes of data appear every day. Express this figure in bytes.
Convert a daily generation of 2.5 quintillion bytes into exabytes.
One exabyte equals 1024 to the power 6 bytes. How many exabytes do 2.5 quintillion bytes make?
Why is the daily volume of Internet data described as colossal?
Estimate the data created in a week if 2.5 quintillion bytes arrive each day.

solution_steps.explain: An exabyte is 1024 to the power 6 bytes.

worked_examples.q: About 2.5 quintillion bytes arise worldwide each day. How many exabytes is that? (1 exabyte = 10^18 bytes.)

concepts.title: Web of Things Single Interface
concepts.definition: The Internet of Things links everyday gadgets so they can exchange data, while its Web of Things extension lets one browser-based interface operate them all, instead of forcing a separate app for every device.
concepts.key_idea: Moving control onto the web collapses a pile of device-specific apps into one interface.
question_patterns: A smart home has 10 devices, each needing its own app. Moving to a Web of Things interface, how many apps are avoided?
Define the Internet of Things in your own words and give two applications.
How are IoT and WoT related to each other?
A user handles 8 gadgets, each with one dedicated app, then switches to a single web interface. How many app installations disappear?
Give two examples of household devices that can join an IoT network.
Why is one common interface more convenient than separate apps for every gadget?

solution_steps.explain: Each gadget needs its own app today.
One web interface replaces the whole pile, so subtract 1.

worked_examples.q: Four smart devices each need their own app today. Under a Web of Things interface, how many apps are needed in total?

concepts.title: Sensors and Smart Cities
concepts.definition: A sensor samples the physical world, such as motion, tilt or tremors, and a smart sensor adds on-board computing so it can process readings before passing them on; city infrastructure stitches such sensors into services like quake-warning buildings and self-reporting bridges.
concepts.key_idea: Accelerometers detect orientation and gyroscopes add rotation detail, which is how a phone flips its display.
question_patterns: Which two sensors let a smartphone know it has been rotated?
How does a smart sensor differ from a plain sensor?
A smart bridge spots a loose bolt. Describe the chain from sensing to alert.
List three city services that a smart city could manage with networked sensors.
What happens inside a phone when you turn it from vertical to horizontal?

solution_steps.explain: Input arrives from the environment, built-in computing interprets it against predefined rules, and only then is a processed alert or command passed onward.

worked_examples.q: Which sensor detects orientation change so a phone can rotate its display?

concepts.title: Pay-per-use Cloud Billing
concepts.definition: Cloud computing rents software, platforms or raw infrastructure over the Internet, and providers bill usage the way an electricity board does: the longer or heavier you use a resource, the more you pay.
concepts.key_idea: On-demand billing spares a new organisation from buying servers before it earns revenue.
question_patterns: A startup rents cloud servers for 400 hours at 8 rupees per hour. Compute the monthly bill.
Why is cloud computing compared with paying for electricity?
A team uses a cloud machine for 120 hours in a month at 10 rupees per hour. What amount is payable?
Distinguish IaaS, PaaS and SaaS with one example of each.
How does cloud storage of data save cost and time for an organisation?
A service bills 5 rupees per hour and is used 300 hours. Find the charge, then the yearly cost if usage stays the same.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the metered hours by the hourly rate.
Repeat the same monthly spend for twelve months.

worked_examples.q: A cloud virtual machine costs Rs 5 per hour and runs 720 hours in a month. What is the month's bill in rupees?

concepts.title: Grid Computing Parallel Speedup
concepts.definition: A grid welds geographically scattered computers, called nodes, into a virtual supercomputer for one large job; splitting the job evenly lets the nodes work simultaneously, so the waiting time shrinks by roughly the node count.
concepts.key_idea: Unlike cloud, which sells services, a grid pools volunteered nodes for a single application-specific goal.
question_patterns: A 100-hour computation is split evenly over 10 grid nodes. How many hours does the job take, and how many are saved?
How does grid computing differ from cloud computing?
A research task of 48 hours divides across 8 nodes. Compute the parallel completion time.
What is a node in a grid, and what is a data grid used for?
Why is a grid called a virtual supercomputer?
Name the middleware-based toolkit mentioned for building grids.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the total job hours by the number of nodes.
Hours saved equal the solo time minus the parallel time.

worked_examples.q: A grid of 10 identical nodes splits a 100-hour job evenly. Roughly how many hours does the job take?

concepts.title: Blockchain Decentralised Ledger
concepts.definition: A blockchain keeps one shared ledger on every participating computer instead of one central database; verified transactions are packed into blocks that append to the chain, so no single member can quietly rewrite history.
concepts.formula: new_block -> all nodes verify -> chain grows
concepts.key_idea: The append-only design means an entry becomes final only when every node authenticates it.
question_patterns: Why is data safer in a blockchain than in a centralised database?
Explain the phrase append-only ledger used for blockchains.
A transaction is requested on a blockchain network. List the steps until it is complete.
Suggest two areas, besides digital currency, where blockchain could improve transparency.
How can blockchain make scholarship distribution accountable?
What does each participating computer hold in a blockchain system?

solution_steps.action: follow a transaction through the chain
solution_steps.explain: A request is broadcast to every node, each node checks it, and only after full agreement does the new block join the shared chain.

worked_examples.q: In a blockchain, verified transactions are packed into what before being appended?

worked_examples.title: Accuracy of a photo-tagging model
worked_examples.problem: A face-tagging model is tried on 400 test photos and errs on 12 of them. Find its accuracy percentage.

steps.explain: Subtract the errors from all trials.
Divide correct trials by all trials.

worked_examples.answer_note: The model scores 97 percent accuracy on the test set.

worked_examples.title: Cloud bill for a small startup
worked_examples.problem: A five-member startup rents a cloud virtual machine for 320 hours in a month at 6 rupees per hour, and keeps this up all year. Find the monthly and yearly cost.

steps.explain: Metered hours times the hourly rate.

worked_examples.answer_note: The startup pays 1920 rupees monthly and 23040 rupees yearly, with no server purchased upfront.
